title: phUSD stable-minter left registered on the buggy old strategies after story-060 (~13,817 DOLA + ~11,936 USDC) — migration-completeness follow-up; minter code is NOT affected by the over-credit bug
contract: lib/phUSD-stable-minter (client position on lib/vault ERC4626YieldStrategy pre-fix builds 0x90ce…7F9 / 0x90af…470)
location: docs/stable-staker-migrations/yield-strategy-swap-June-12-2026.md 'Scope' section (staker-only); no suite script repoints the minter to the V2 strategies

scopedAnalysisOutcome.verdict: NO minter-side code fix needed or possible. The over-credit bug cannot harm PhusdStableMinter: (1) mint() issues phUSD = amount * exchangeRate * decimalAdjust (calculateMintAmount, PhusdStableMinter.sol:243-256) and never reads principalOf/totalBalanceOf/_positionValue, so over-credited principal cannot mint unbacked phUSD; (2) there is no redemption path (story-007 removed withdraw; no withdraw/redeem/burn), so 'distorts minter redemptions' is moot; (3) the minter holds no levers over strategy accounting (only deposit()) — position movement is strategy-owner-side (withdrawAsOwner/totalWithdrawal/relinquishPrincipalAsOwner/emergencyWithdraw). Residual effect on the minter is conservative: skimSurplus understates the minter's surplus and under-skims, never over-skims.
scopedAnalysisOutcome.reclassification: Provisional Medium (minter-side referral) -> Low (migration-completeness follow-up, owned by the strategy/migration side). Not a minter-code vulnerability and not independently exploitable.

description: The story-060 suite repoints only the StableStaker client to the V2 strategies; nothing re-registers the phUSD minter. On fork the minter holds 13,816.56 DOLA and 11,935.65 USDC of recorded principal on the buggy old strategies (~13x/6x the staker's exposure). The scoped analysis requested by this referral is now complete: the minter is architecturally immune to the over-credit bug (decoupled minting, no redeem path). The remaining issue is operational migration completeness: (a) fresh user mints keep routing into a known-buggy strategy, and (b) once the staker is evacuated first at an over-credited basis from the shared 'underwater' pool, the residual below-par shortfall can be left with the minter. Both are fixed by repointing the minter onto the V2 strategies (and optionally consolidating its position) — strategy/migration-side, no minter code change.
impact: Until a follow-up migration runs, the minter keeps depositing new user collateral into a known-buggy strategy and its existing ~13.8k DOLA / ~11.9k USDC position can absorb the shared pool's below-par shortfall. No unbacked phUSD can be minted and no redemption is distorted (the minter has neither read-back nor redeem).

classification.assetImpact: No direct asset loss attributable to minter code. phUSD issuance is decoupled from strategy principal and there is no redemption path. Backing-health only: existing minter principal remains on a strategy whose accounting overstates it, and new mints keep flowing there until a repoint migration runs.
attackPath: Not an attack path. Operational completeness gap: the migration suite migrated only the staker client, leaving the minter on the old buggy strategies.

Consequence (a): mint() -> deposit() keeps crediting nominal principal into 0x90ce.../0x90af... (over-credit defect persists for the minter, but phUSD over-mint is impossible since issuance ignores strategy principal).

Consequence (b): with the staker evacuated first at over-credited principal from the shared underwater pool, the residual shortfall is left with the minter (realized via strategy withdraw mechanics + migration ordering, not minter code).
classification.likelihood: N/A (operational). Materiality of (b) depends on whether the autopool is genuinely below par; (a) is certain until the repoint runs.
classification.assumptions: Owner of old strategies, V2 strategies, and the minter is the deployer multisig/EOA; YS-01 (previewRedeem brick) is fixed before the V2 strategies are usable.
classification.externalRequirements: A follow-up migration that repoints the minter to ysDolaV2/ysUsdcV2 (and optionally consolidates its position). See plan.

evidence: Source: PhusdStableMinter.sol mint()/calculateMintAmount (L203-256) reads no strategy state; no withdraw/redeem/burn (story-007 'Remove buggy withdraw'). AYieldStrategy principal/withdraw/skim semantics confirm conservative under-skim and owner-only position movement. Fork reads: YS_DOLA_OLD.principalOf(DOLA, minter)==13816564202291221245191; YS_USDC_OLD.principalOf(USDC, minter)==11935645684. side-effects.json clusterChecks[5].
recommendation: No change to PhusdStableMinter. Extend the migration (preferred: repoint the EXISTING minter, no new minter needed): for each token, ysTV2.setClient(minter,true); minter.registerStablecoin(T, ysTV2, rate, decimals); minter.approveYS(T, ysTV2); minter.setMaxMintPerDay(T, <live cap>) — re-applying the cap that registerStablecoin silently zeroes. Optionally consolidate the existing position: strategy-owner withdrawAsOwner(minter, operator, principalOf(minter)) then minter.noMintDeposit(ysTV2, T, recovered). Run after Leg 2/Reset, with the minter as sole remaining client. Full sequence, post-conditions, the registerStablecoin cap-reset footgun, and the rejected new-minter alternative are in reports/phoenix-phase-2-staging/12/script-audits/migrate:ys-swap-deploy/YS-12-minter-followup-plan.md.
dedupNotes: Sole source: deploy F8 (idx7). Originally KEPT VISIBLE as a REFERRAL per Law 1; the routed scoped analysis of phUSD-stable-minter is now complete (minter immune; see scopedAnalysisOutcome). Same scope-gap family as YS-03 (suite migrated only the staker client).
sanitizationReason: Scoped /analyze of phUSD-stable-minter complete (2026-06-12): minter code is unaffected by the over-credit bug (decoupled mint, no redeem path, no levers). Reclassified from provisional Medium referral to Low migration-completeness follow-up owned by the strategy/migration side. Not submitted as a minter-side H/M; tracked as a Low operational footgun.
severityJustification: Low: no minter-code vulnerability and not independently exploitable. The exposure is a migration-completeness footgun (minter left on a known-buggy strategy; new mints keep flowing there; residual shared-pool shortfall can land on the minter), remediated operationally by a repoint migration. No unbacked phUSD can be minted and no redemption is distorted.
